newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday August 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday August 4.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Democratic party of the Left leader Massimo D'Alema said the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, which gives Italy's centre-left government a parliamentary majority, is "still not fully reliable". D'Alema warned Refoundation "must stay in the majority, but without being the determinant factor." (La Stampa)
* Italy's main unions Cgil and Cisl are at odds over a proposal to lower the minimum wage as a solution to rampant unemployment in the south. (Corriere della Sera)

* Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco announces in an interview over the weekend an overhaul of Italy's taxation system, including new ways to fight evasion will get underway in the autumn (La Stampa, Il Messaggero)
* European financial markets are anxious over the dollar's high level (all).

* With the cashfall from British Airports Authority's purchase of the majority stake in Naples' Capodichino airport, authorities plan a complete modernisation of the airport, including a underground railway stop, new shopping centre and a refurbishing of the waiting rooms. A new direct Naples-London flight is also planned.
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
